subtopics.title: Conservation of mass

slots.X: A carbonate sample loses mass when heated in an open test tube. Why is conservation not violated?
slots.Y: When a candle burns in a closed vessel, why doesn't the mass simply vanish as the wax disappears? A mass law applies to a chosen system boundary, including gases, liquids and solids, while products can have different appearances.
slots.Z: Burning 12 g carbon with 32 g oxygen in a sealed reaction produces 44 g CO₂ with the same atoms.
slots.W: Learner independently performs the decisive EXPLAIN inference required by: A carbonate sample loses mass when heated in an open test tube. Why is conservation not violated?

qrt_instances.student_task: A carbonate sample loses mass when heated in an open test tube. Why is conservation not violated?
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: The mass after a reaction equals the mass of the solid products only.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Include every phase in the same weighed system.
qrt_instances.visual_job: Put reaction vessel and surrounding gas inside a dashed system boundary. Draw arrows for gas crossing only when the container is open. Use colour-coded elemental atom counts on both sides.

slots.X: Balance Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃ without changing the product formula.
slots.Y: When a candle burns in a closed vessel, why doesn't the mass simply vanish as the wax disappears? Equation coefficients multiply entire chemical formulas; subscripts define molecule composition and must not be altered for balancing.
slots.Z: For H₂ + O₂ → H₂O, use 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O; the H and O atom counts match.

subtopics.title: Constant composition and Dalton theory

slots.X: Why do pure-water samples from different sources have the same hydrogen/oxygen mass ratio despite different total impurities?
slots.Y: Why is pure water described by H₂O whether collected from rain, a river or a laboratory? Compound identity persists even when its surrounding mixture varies; impurities are separate components.
slots.Z: Rainwater and seawater each contain H₂O molecules; the salts in seawater do not convert pure H₂O into a different molecule.
slots.W: Learner independently performs the decisive EXPLAIN inference required by: Why do pure-water samples from different sources have the same hydrogen/oxygen mass ratio despite different total impurities?

qrt_instances.student_task: Why do pure-water samples from different sources have the same hydrogen/oxygen mass ratio despite different total impurities?
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: The two hydrogen atoms mean water contains twice the mass of hydrogen as oxygen.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Explicitly state whether a ratio counts atoms or mass.
qrt_instances.visual_job: Compare H₂O molecular diagrams from two samples; add free salt ions in one sample to show impurities without altering H₂O connectivity.

subtopics.title: Chemical symbols and electron-dot introduction

slots.X: Why does magnesium's Lewis symbol typically have two dots even though neutral Mg has 12 electrons?
slots.Y: What does a single dot around a chemical symbol stand for in an electron-dot diagram? The electron configuration identifies how many valence electrons a dot symbol should show.
slots.Z: O has 2,6, so six dots, not eight. Mg has 2,8,2, so two outer dots.
slots.W: Learner independently performs the decisive EXPLAIN inference required by: Why does magnesium's Lewis symbol typically have two dots even though neutral Mg has 12 electrons?

qrt_instances.student_task: Why does magnesium's Lewis symbol typically have two dots even though neutral Mg has 12 electrons?
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: Each dot shows an atom's entire electron inventory.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Distinguish full electron configuration from outer-shell dot count.
